title: Fridge Organization Ideas So Food Stops Going Bad in the Back
description: Easy fridge organization for ADHD brains: zones, an eat-first bin and 7 Amazon finds so you see your food and waste less of it.
intro:
We've all done it. You open a container in the back of the fridge, and it's... alive. You don't remember buying it. You don't remember cooking it. It has become a science experiment.

For our brains, the fridge is a perfect storm. Food goes in, goes behind other food and stops existing. Then we buy more because we can't see what we have, and the cycle repeats.

A few simple changes fix most of it. Here's how to set up a fridge that shows you what you've got.

sections.heading: The principle: visible and front
sections.body:
Everything in the fridge should either be visible from the front or in a clear bin you can slide out. If you have to move three things to see a fourth, the fourth is going to spoil.

That's it. That's the whole philosophy. Everything else is how to make it happen.

sections.heading: Step 1: Quick clean-out (15 minutes)
sections.body:
Do this right before a grocery trip, when the fridge is at its emptiest.

- Toss anything expired, moldy or mysterious.
- Combine duplicates (three open jars of the same salsa, anyone?).
- Wipe the shelves with a damp cloth.

Don't aim for spotless. A quick wipe is enough.

sections.heading: Step 2: Set up simple zones
sections.body:
- **Top shelf:** ready-to-eat stuff like leftovers, yogurt and snacks.
- **Middle shelf:** dairy, eggs and drinks.
- **Bottom shelf:** raw meat, in a bin, so it can't drip on anything.
- **Drawers:** produce.
- **Door:** condiments.

Use clear bins to hold each group. Bins make the fridge work like drawers, which is way easier for our brains than stacks.

sections.heading: Step 3: Make an 'eat first' bin
sections.body:
This is the single most useful trick. One clear bin, labeled **EAT FIRST**, right at eye level. Anything that needs eating soon goes in it: leftovers, half an onion, the berries that are about to turn.

When anyone's hungry, they check the bin first. Less waste, and you stop finding week-old lasagna in the back.

sections.heading: Step 4: Keep produce where you'll see it
sections.body:
Crisper drawers are where good intentions go to die. If you keep forgetting vegetables, try moving them to a clear produce container on a middle shelf. When you see them, you use them.

Wash and chop a few things after grocery shopping if you have the energy. If not, buy pre-cut. That's not cheating. That's a system that works with your life.

sections.heading: Step 5: Label the shelves
sections.body: A label on the shelf or bin ("SNACKS", "DAIRY", "EAT FIRST") means everyone in the house knows where things go when they put groceries away. It keeps the system working even when you're not the one unpacking.

sections.heading: The weekly 2-minute check
sections.body: Before you write your grocery list, open the fridge and look at the eat-first bin and each zone. What needs eating? What's running low? This two-minute check saves money and makes the list faster, too.
